reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR introduces a new “predictive sufficiency” evaluation module for the transformerless pipeline, enabling divergence (teacher vs depth-reduced graph) and rate–distortion reporting across graph depths, along with CBOR serialization and basic tests. **Changes:** - Added `transformerless::predictive_sufficiency` with `GraphDepth`, divergence metrics, and `RateDistortionReport` CBOR round-tripping. - Extended `OpKernel` to be serializable/clonable/comparable so it can be embedded in reports. - Added a new test suite covering divergence computations, depth evaluation, and CBOR round-trip. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/predictive_sufficiency.rs | New module implementing divergence metrics and rate–distortion reporting + CBOR serialization. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/runtime.rs | Adds derives to `OpKernel` to support report serialization and comparisons. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/mod.rs | Exposes the new `predictive_sufficiency` module (non-wasm). | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/predictive_sufficiency_test.rs | New tests for KL/cross-entropy, depth evaluation, and CBOR round-trip. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. review_comments.body: `compute_kl_divergence` clamps `pi` to `eps`, which makes terms with true `P(i)=0` contribute non-zero mass and biases KL (e.g., KL(P||P) can become >0 for distributions containing zeros). It also uses natural-log but later code/docs describe KL in bits.

`compute_cross_entropy` clamps `pi` to `eps`, so events with true `P(i)=0` still contribute to the sum (biasing cross-entropy). If cross-entropy is intended in bits (as suggested by the rate/distortion doc), use log2 and only clamp `q`.
The `0.1` ops-to-bytes scaling factor is an unexplained magic number. Extract it to a named constant so its meaning is discoverable and easy to tune consistently.
`partial_cmp(...).unwrap()` will panic if any probability is NaN. These inputs are floating-point model outputs, so this should be made robust (e.g., ignore non-finite values) rather than crashing.

`top5_recall` is currently hardcoded to `1.0`, which makes the metric misleading/meaningless in the report output. Either compute it from inputs (define what it means here) or remove the field until it can be populated correctly.
`intermediate` and `full` are unused, which will trigger unused-variable warnings (and likely fail the repo’s `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` check). Prefix with `_` or remove them.

The KL/cross-entropy tests don’t cover the important edge case where `P(i)=0` and/or `Q(i)=0`. Adding a zero-mass case catches biases introduced by epsilon-clamping and ensures KL(P||P) stays exactly ~0 when zeros are present.
Implemented top-five recall from the teacher argmax and graph top-five predictions, with hit/miss coverage in 9e6a5d7.
